subject: EU fraud hold: 14-day debug hold request + proof-of-delete and CAIQ/SIG mapping
messages:
From: Marta Larsen <marta.larsen@nordictrust.bank>
To: lauren_bishop@redwood.ai
Cc: compliance@nordictrust.bank
Date: 2026-10-17T08:12:00+01:00
Subject: Request: 14-day debug hold for fraud flagged sessions + deletion proof

Hi Lauren,

Thanks for the call earlier. As discussed, our fraud investigations team runs expedited reviews that sometimes require access to ephemeral debug/session traces beyond the default window. We'd like to request a customer-scoped carveout for accounts that hit our fraud flag. The specifics:

- Scope: session debug traces and K/V inference cache for tenant IDs under NordicTrust (tenant: nordic-001).
- Hold window: 14 days after the flagged event (not rolling for all sessions).
- Trigger: our webhook to Redwood with a signed event ID (we will provide HMAC key).
- Audit/evidence: we need a machine-readable deletion manifest showing object ids, SHA256 hashes, deletion timestamp, and who initiated the deletion (redwood system account id).
- Certifications: CAIQ/SIG mapping items around data flows and proof-of-delete runbook (SOC 2 control references would also be helpful).

Can you confirm whether Redwood can: 1) implement a tenant-scoped hold triggered by our webhook, 2) produce the deletion manifest we requested programmatically, and 3) provide the CAIQ/SIG artifacts that map to the deletion workflow?

We attached our SIG questions (PDF) — please respond with a proposed timeline so we can coordinate internal approvals.

Appreciate it,
Marta
Head of Compliance Operations
NordicTrust Bank

--
Attachment: NordicTrust_SIG_Questions.pdf
From: lauren_bishop@redwood.ai
To: Marta Larsen <marta.larsen@nordictrust.bank>
Cc: irene_choi@redwood.ai, karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-10-17T12:45:00+01:00
Subject: Re: Request: 14-day debug hold for fraud flagged sessions + deletion proof

Marta —

Thanks, this is clear and reasonable. Short answers up-front: yes on tenant-scoped holds, yes on programmatic deletion manifests, and yes we can produce CAIQ/SIG artifacts that call out the deletion workflow. Below I mapped next steps and open questions so we can scope the work and deliverables.

What we will deliver
- Technical spec for tenant-triggered hold + webhook verification (HMAC) — target delivery: 2026-10-22.
- Deletion manifest format (CSV + JSON schema) and sample manifest export — target 2026-10-24.
- CAIQ/SIG items and SOC 2 control mapping that reference the deletion runbook (with redwood internal playbook excerpt) — target 2026-10-27.

Open questions for you
1) Forensics scope: do you need raw KV cache blobs or just parsed session traces and request/response artifacts?
2) Retention exceptions: will the 14d hold be automatically applied only after your webhook call, or do you also want Redwood to support manual opens from your Support/CS team?
3) Evidence delivery cadence: do you prefer a push URL for manifests or periodic packaged deliveries to your secure Drive?

Irene and Karthik are on copy — Irene will coordinate CAIQ/SIG artifacts and legal wording; Karthik will confirm implementation constraints on retention tagging and manifests.

I'll schedule a short follow-up call for Tuesday to walk through the spec draft.

Best,
Lauren Bishop
Director, Security & Compliance
Redwood Inference

--
Attachment: redwood-retention-tagging-overview.pdf
From: karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
To: lauren_bishop@redwood.ai
Cc: Marta Larsen <marta.larsen@nordictrust.bank>, irene_choi@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-10-18T09:22:00+01:00
Subject: Re: Request: 14-day debug hold for fraud flagged sessions + deletion proof

Marta, Lauren —

Adding technical detail on how we would implement the tenant-triggered hold and the manifest generation. High-level design:

1) Tagging model: when NordicTrust sends the HMAC-authenticated webhook with event type FRAUD_FLAG and event id, Redwood will tag affected artifacts with a "nordic-001:fraud_hold:<event_id>" retention tag. That tag overrides the default ephemeral policy for those objects to a 14-day retention window from the event timestamp.

2) Storage and isolation: tagged artifacts will remain in tenant-scoped buckets with role-based access. Only our forensic export service (read-only role) and your signed webhook can lift or create holds.

3) Manifest export: we will support both an on-demand manifest endpoint (authenticated with a short-lived token) and scheduled zips to your secure Drive. The manifest will include: object_id, object_path, object_type (kv-cache/session-trace/log), sha256, created_at, retention_tag, deletion_scheduled_at, deletion_completed_at (null until deleted). Example CSV attached (redwood-delete-manifest-example.csv).

4) Proof-of-delete: when deletion completes, the manifest entry will be updated with deletion_completed_at and a deletion_receipt signed by Redwood's HSM key (we will provide a verification endpoint to validate signature).

5) Privacy guardrails: we will only persist raw KV/cache blobs for objects that meet a size/entropy threshold and that are strictly required for forensic reconstruction. If NordicTrust needs raw blobs for a specific investigation, we recommend a short-lived export to your S3 with a strict TTL.

Constraints and timeline
- Implementation of the webhook/tagging + manifest endpoint is approximately 3 sprints (6 weeks) if scoped as tenant-level feature with onboarding. We can front-load a minimal MVP (on-demand manifest + manual hold API) in ~3 weeks.
- For the HSM-signed deletion receipts and SOC 2 evidence mapping, we will need coordination with Security and Legal — estimate 4–6 weeks to finalize formal artifacts.

Questions for Marta
- Does NordicTrust require the deletion receipt to be verifiable offline (i.e., a signed blob you can archive)?
- For forensic exports to your S3/Drive, can we use the same endpoint you currently use for incident exports (you pointed to it on our last call)?

Happy to demo the manifest endpoint prototype during the follow-up call.

Thanks,
Karthik Iyer
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

--
Attachment: redwood-delete-manifest-example.csv
From: Marta Larsen <marta.larsen@nordictrust.bank>
To: lauren_bishop@redwood.ai
Cc: irene_choi@redwood.ai, karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-10-19T16:34:00+01:00
Subject: Re: Request: 14-day debug hold for fraud flagged sessions + deletion proof

Lauren / Karthik —

This looks good and covers the core asks. Quick responses:
- We only need parsed session traces and request/response artifacts for the initial phase, but reserve the right to request raw KV blobs on a per-investigation basis (S3 temp export is fine).
- Yes, deletion receipts must be verifiable offline — we will archive them with case records.
- Delivery: prefer on-demand manifest endpoint initially; once stable, move to nightly push zips to our secure drive.

Approvals: I have internal sign-off to proceed with the MVP (on-demand manifest + manual hold API). Please treat the HSM-signed receipts as high priority for evidence integrity.

Next steps:
1) Draft spec & webhook HMAC details from Redwood by 2026-10-22 (as Lauren indicated).
2) Demo manifest endpoint and provide sample signed receipt during follow-up (we are available 2026-10-23 10:00–12:00 CET).
3) Once MVP validated, we will schedule legal/contract addendum for formal retention carveout.

Thanks for the quick turnaround.

Best,
Marta
Head of Compliance Operations
NordicTrust Bank
